scoring_justification: Checker recomputes key features (yield stress, crystallinity min/max, S_global threshold, affine stretch, g shifts) from raw CSV artifacts and compares to paper-reported values with generous tolerances.

hidden_assets.purpose: paper gold reference values for yield stress, crystallinity initial, S_global, stretch, and g second peak positions
hidden_assets.source_provenance: paper Figures 3,10,11,7 and text, as approximated in solve.sh
hidden_assets.generation_method: extracted from paper descriptions and synthetic solve.sh output
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: values are taken from the paper's reported results (crystallinity 0.425, yield stress ~0.75, etc.)

schema.description: Stress-strain curves for semicrystalline and amorphous samples.

outputs.description: True stress versus true strain for both samples at T=0.2. The checker will recompute yield stress, verify strain-softening/hardening trends.

schema.description: Crystallinity fraction X_C and global nematic order parameter S_global as functions of strain.

outputs.description: The checker will verify that X_C initially decreases then increases, and S_global rises above 0.5 at high strain, with tolerances bound to paper-reported values.

schema.description: Comparison of macroscopic draw ratio λ and effective microscopic chain stretch λ_eff.

outputs.description: The checker will verify λ_eff ≈ λ for λ ≲ 2 and sub-affine deviation beyond.

schema.description: Pair distribution function g(ρ,0) and g(0,y) in crystalline regions.

outputs.description: The checker will verify that the second nearest-neighbor peak in g(ρ,0) shifts to smaller distances at strains <0.8 and stabilises.

schema.description: Pair distribution function g(ρ,0) and g(0,y) in amorphous regions.

outputs.description: The checker will verify that the amorphous g(ρ,0) second peak remains largely constant until strain ~0.8.

output_contract.notes: Scoring uses metric recomputation from the raw CSV artifacts against hidden gold curves extracted from the paper at T=0.2. Tolerances are generous (±20% for stress, ±0.05 for crystallinity, ±0.1 for S_global) to absorb stochastic and implementation variance. All scored artifacts are required for a full reward.
